title: Glass menus and native menu bridge
summary: PopupMenu (context and sub-menus with keyboard model), MenuBar over MenuDef[], trimMenu/setMenuStyle for Edit > Menus, and NativeMenus that mirrors the same defs into the macOS native menu bar through Tauri. Menu items are command ids resolved through a Commands object.
description: Menus are data: `MenuItem = commandId | "-" | {label, items}`. `PopupMenu` builds its panel once and `setItems` patches it; `MenuBar` hosts the top-level defs and does not open from the keyboard while a dialog is open (`anyDialogOpen`). On macOS desktop `wantsNativeMenus()` is true unless the user keeps menus in the window (`formvis.menusInWindow`), and `NativeMenus` builds Tauri native menus from the same defs; Edit keys go to a focused text field through the shell `text_edit` command. The glass look lives in `panels.css` (`cv-menu*`). Imports `./commands` (Commands) and `./i18n`, which are not seeded in this corpus.
statusReason: seeded from B06 for the owner to confirm

exports.doc: A command id, a separator, or a submenu of further items.

exports.signature: export interface SubMenu { label: string; items: MenuItem[] }
exports.doc: A submenu item: a label and its own item list.
Commands that stay in the menus whatever is hidden, so the way back is never lost.

exports.signature: export function setMenuStyle(hidden: readonly string[], colors: Record<string, string>): void
exports.doc: Sets the command ids hidden from the menus and the colour name per item (Edit > Menus).
Items without the hidden commands; a submenu left empty goes too, and no separator is left leading, trailing or doubled.
One menu panel (also used as a context menu): keyboard model, sub-menus, relabel on language change.

exports.signature: export interface MenuDef { label: string; items: MenuItem[] | (() => MenuItem[]) }
exports.doc: A menubar menu: its label and its items; a function is called afresh each time the menu opens.
The top menu bar: one button and PopupMenu per MenuDef; opens on click or hover when another is open.
Rebuilds the panel rows from a MenuItem list.
Refreshes labels, checks and enabled states, then shows the menu at `x, y`, kept within the window; a menu taller than the window scrolls.
Re-labels every row and submenu in place after a language change; only text changes, no node is rebuilt.
Closes the panel and its open sub-menu.
Opens menu i; keyboard true returns focus to the previous element on close.
Closes the open menu.
Formvis's menus in the macOS menu bar when it runs as the desktop app (Phase 21, UI_SPEC.md section 2: the target's menus are the system's).
The person's choice to keep the menus in the window on macOS (View > Menus in Window); it applies at the next start.
True when the user chose to keep menus in the window (stored under formvis.menusInWindow).

exports.signature: export function accelerator(combo: string | undefined): string | null
exports.doc: Formvis's key combo ('Mod+Shift+S') as a Tauri accelerator ('CmdOrCtrl+Shift+S'); null for what Tauri has no name for.
True when a text-editing element has focus, so Edit keys go to it.
Builds Tauri native menus from the same MenuDef list and refreshes check and enabled state.
Builds (or rebuilds) the menu bar; later calls while one is building are folded into one more build.
The enabled and tick states, refreshed a moment after the app changes (grouped, so a burst of changes is one pass).

invariants.text: Build a node once, then patch text, classes, hidden flags and lists in place. Never assign innerHTML or clear textContent on a live container to rebuild it, and reserve space so nothing shifts when content arrives.
User-visible strings go through t() from the i18n module; the English text is the key.
Icons are inline currentColor SVG strings from the icons module (icon(name, size)); no icon library, and the three-star sparkle icon is banned under any name.
Menu items are command ids; labels, keys and enabled state come from the Commands object so menus, palette and shortcuts cannot disagree.
The ids in MENU_KEEP (edit-menus, shortcuts, settings) stay in the menus whatever the user hides.
